title: Cyclotomic fields
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: A small nonzero integer in all Stickelberger ideals via Voronoi's congruence
modules.note:
The analytic input to the bound for the odd part of Ш: one nonzero integer X of controlled size
that, times c ^ (e + 1) - 1, lies in all the Stickelberger ideals for N and e.

* `New.OddPart.IsStickelbergerBound`: the two properties required of X, as a structure.
* `New.OddPart.exists_isStickelbergerBound`: such an X exists with X ≤ 2 ^ (N + e + 3) ^ 6, for
  e ≥ 1.

The idea: the generalised Bernoulli numbers of all characters mod N, corrected where they vanish for
reasons of parity, are the eigenvalues of one integer matrix. Its determinant is nonzero
(`New.OddPart.sum_mul_bernoulli_ne_zero`), is divisible by each eigenvalue, and is bounded by
the Fourier series of the Bernoulli polynomial. Voronoi's congruence
(`New.OddPart.voronoi_congruence_bernoulli`) links the Bernoulli numbers to the Stickelberger sums;
it rests on a congruence for power sums along an arithmetic progression
(`New.OddPart.exists_sq_dvd_factorial_mul_sum_pow_sub`).
modules.literature:
Known result: Voronoi's congruence for twisted power sums and the trivial zeros of Dirichlet
L-functions. Here the congruence is twisted by a possibly imprimitive character and stated for power
sums. One non-zero integer with an explicit size bound has the following property. For c ≡ 1 mod N,
(c ^ (e + 1) - 1) X is congruent, modulo every m prime to c, to 2 w times the twisted Stickelberger
sum, where w does not depend on m. This holds for every character ψ with ψ(-1) = -(-1) ^ e and
values in a domain of characteristic 0. In addition, for every prime l, some c ≡ 1 mod N prime to l
has (c ^ e - 1) (c ^ (e + 1) - 1) ∣ X. Source: K. Ireland, M. Rosen, A Classical Introduction to
Modern Number Theory, 2nd ed. 1990; for the untwisted statement also M. Eberl, Kummer's congruence,
Archive of Formal Proofs 2024.

modules.title: A weak form of Stickelberger's theorem for Gauss sums, and a family of Jacobi-type quotients
modules.note:
Gauss sums over `𝔽_p` give a family of elements `J x` of `Ωˣ`, `Ω = ℚ̄`, indexed by torsion points
`x` of `ℚ/ℤ`, with a known Galois action and a distribution relation up to elements of finite order.

* `New.OddPart.floorDiff`, `New.OddPart.sum_floorDiff`: the integer `⌊c ⟨x⟩⌋ - ⌊c ⟨-x⟩⌋` and its
  distribution relation (Hermite's identity).
* `New.OddPart.exists_galUnitsRep_gaussSum_eq`, `New.OddPart.stickelberger`: Galois action on Gauss
  sums, and their orders at a place `B` above `p`.
* `New.OddPart.exists_isJacobiFamily`: the family `J`, built from the quotients
  `j t = g(χ) ^ c / g(χ ^ c)` as `j t / j (-t)`.

Notions from other files:
* `Ω` is `ℚ̄`, and `DiscreteUnits Ω` is `Ωˣ` written additively: a sum is a product, `c • u` is
  `u ^ c`. `galUnitsRep σ` is the action of `σ ∈ Gal(Ω/ℚ)` on it.
* `ClosurePlace`: a valuation subring `B` of `Ω`; it lies above `p` when `B.valuation p < 1`, and
  `centrePrime Ω B` is the prime ideal of `𝓞 Ω` that it defines; `principalUnits B` is the subgroup
  of `DiscreteUnits Ω` of the `u` with `B.valuation (u - 1) < 1`, that is `u ≡ 1` at `B`.
* `ordRat ℚ B u`: the order of `u` at `B`, normalised so that a prime `p` below `B` has order one.
* `cyclotomicCharMod Ω N σ`: the cyclotomic character of `σ` modulo `N`, the unit `a` with
  `σ ζ = ζ ^ a` for every `N`-th root of unity `ζ`.
* `New.QZ`: the group `ℚ/ℤ`; `New.QZ.fracRep x = ⟨x⟩` is the representative in `[0, 1)`, and
  `New.QZ.ofZMod r b = b / r`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Stickelberger's factorisation of Gauss sums and the Davenport–Hasse product relation.
Here only prime fields are treated, and characters are named by the valuation of their Gauss sum.
The product relation is proved for Jacobi-type quotients of Gauss sums and only up to a root of
unity. Source: L. Washington, Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields, 2nd ed. 1997, 6.2 and Thm 15.1; for
the product relation, H. Davenport, H. Hasse, J. reine angew. Math. 172 (1935).

modules.title: Detecting unramified cocycles and a uniform bound for a model of the odd part of Ш. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.note:
Let E be a number field inside ℚ(μ_N) and let l be a prime. Polynomially many elements of the
absolute Galois group of E detect the locally constant cocycles of a Tate twist that take values in
O / lⁿ and are unramified outside l. For a CM field E inside ℚ(μ_N), this gives one integer X of
explicit size whose valuation bounds the length of a module of odd cocycles at every prime l.

## Overview of this theory

For a CM field `E` inside `ℚ(μ_N)`, and `O` the integers of a finite extension of `ℚ_ℓ` with enough
roots of unity for the characters mod `N`, `New.Selmer.shaOdd` is a module of cocycles of `Gal(Ω/E)`
with values in `O/ℓⁿ(-e)`, modelled on the odd part of `Ш¹(E, O/ℓⁿ(-e))`; no comparison with `Ш¹` is
proved. For `e = 0` it consists of the everywhere unramified homomorphisms. Here `ℓ` is a prime and
`e, n ≥ 0`.

* `New.exists_length_shaOdd_le`: for each `t ≥ 0` there is an integer `X`, depending on `E`, `N` and
  `t`, with `0 < X ≤ 2^(4T²⁷) h_E`. Here `T = N + t + 3` and `h_E` is the class number of `E`. The
  length of `New.Selmer.shaOdd` over `O` is at most `v_O(X)` for all `ℓ`, `O`, `n` and all `e < t`.

No equality of characteristic ideals (the main conjecture of Mazur and Wiles) is proved.

Proof outline: 1. `Voronoi`: `New.OddPart.exists_isStickelbergerBound` gives, for `e ≥ 1`, an
integer `0 < X ≤ 2^((N+e+3)⁶)` satisfying `New.OddPart.IsStickelbergerBound N e X`. This is a
bounded divisibility of twisted Stickelberger sums.

2. `Stickelberger`: `New.OddPart.exists_isJacobiFamily` fixes a prime `p`, a place `B` above `p` and
   any `c ∈ ℕ`. It builds a map `J` from `ℚ/ℤ` to units, a variant of Jacobi sums. For `p ≡ 1 mod M`
   and `Mx = 0`, `J(x)` is a unit at places not above `p`. It has absolute value one in every
   complex embedding. Its order at `B` is `New.OddPart.floorDiff c x`. It also satisfies Galois and
   product relations.
3. `Kolyvagin.DerivativeCocycles`: `New.OddPart.exists_isKolyvaginSystem` builds
   `cyc^(e+1)ψ`-cocycles `κ_S : G_ℚ → O/ℓⁿ`. Here `cyc` is the `ℓ`-adic cyclotomic character and `ψ`
   a Dirichlet character mod `N`. The sets `S` range over subsets of a finite set `P` of primes
   `≡ 1 mod cNℓⁿ`, and `p ≡ 1 mod Nℓⁿ∏P`. For `q ∈ P ∖ S` and a place `A` above `q`, the value of
   `κ_S` at a Frobenius at `A` is a value of `κ_{S∪{q}}` on inertia at `A`.
4. `Kolyvagin.ReciprocityComponentBounds`: take `e ≥ 1` and `cycᵉψ` odd. Then `4X²` kills
   `New.OddPart.component`, a set of cocycles `G_ℚ → O/ℓ^ν` attached to `cycᵉψ`
   (`New.OddPart.nsmul_component_eq_zero`, an analogue of Stickelberger's theorem). If moreover
   `ℓ > N + e + 3`, there are `v_ℓ(X) + 1` elements of `G_ℚ` with the following property: a cocycle
   in the component vanishing at all of them is zero
   (`New.OddPart.exists_detecting_points_component`).
5. `OddSha`: for `e > 0`, the group is split by characters `ψ`, and step 4 gives an integer killing
   `New.Selmer.shaOdd`. A bounded number of suitable elements of `G_E` suffice to test whether a
   cocycle is zero. For small `ℓ` this uses ray classes, and for large `ℓ` it uses step 4. Together
   these bound the length. For `e = 0`, the class number `h_E` serves.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.OddPart.exists_detecting_points_cocycles`: the detecting set and the bound on its size.
* `New.OddPart.nsmul_shaOdd_eq_zero_of_isStickelbergerBound`: an integer that kills
  `New.Selmer.shaOdd` for e ≠ 0, at every prime l.
* `New.OddPart.length_shaOdd_le_of_le_sq`, `New.OddPart.length_shaOdd_le_of_sq_lt`: the bounds on
  the length for small and for large primes l.

Notions from other files:
* `Ω`: the fixed algebraic closure of ℚ; `Gal(Ω/E)` is its group of automorphisms
  over `E`, the absolute Galois group of `E`.
* `New.Selmer.tateTwist`: the rank-one representation O(−e), the character cyc^{−e} with values in
  O, as 1 × 1 matrices.
* `New.conjGal`: the endomorphism g ↦ c g c of Gal(Ω / E), where c is `New.cmConj`, the complex
  conjugation fixed in Gal(Ω / ℚ); a cocycle z is odd if z (c g c) = -z g.
modules.literature:
For large `l` a bound of this kind follows from the Iwasawa main conjecture of Mazur and Wiles; only
an upper bound for the length at finite level, by an integer of explicit size, is proved here. One
non-zero integer serves at all primes, 2 included; small primes are handled by a crude count of
generators of the ray class group. Source: B. Mazur, A. Wiles, Class fields of abelian extensions of
Q, Invent. Math. 76 (1984); C. Greither, Ann. Inst. Fourier 42 (1992), Thm 3.2.

modules.title: Kolyvagin's derivative cocycles from Gauss sums, for one set of primes
modules.group: Kolyvagin cocycles, reciprocity laws and class bounds
modules.note:
The main result, `New.OddPart.exists_isKolyvaginSystem`, constructs Kolyvagin's cocycles `κ S` with
values in `O/lⁿ` from the Jacobi-type quotients `J` of `New.OddPart.exists_isJacobiFamily`. One
takes `lⁿ`-th roots `y` of `J`, forms the roots of unity `γ y / (g γ g⁻¹) y`, applies the derivative
operators at the primes of `S` and sums against `aᵉ ψ(a)`. The local properties are read modulo a
place, where roots of unity of order prime to it stay distinct.

* `New.OddPart.IsKolyvaginSystem`: the properties of the cocycles `κ S`.
* `New.OddPart.exists_isKolyvaginSystem`: a Kolyvagin system exists.
* `New.OddPart.derivativeSum`: the derivative operators followed by the character sum.

Conventions: `Ω = ℚ̄` is an algebraic closure of `ℚ`, and its places are valuation subrings
(`ClosurePlace`); `DiscreteUnits Ω` is `Ω^×` written additively, so `n • u` is `uⁿ`, and
`galUnitsRep g` is the action of `g` on it; `New.QZ.ofZMod M a` is `a/M` in `ℚ/ℤ`;
`QuotSpan (l ^ n : O)` is `O/lⁿ`; `floorDiff c x` is `⌊c ⟨x⟩⌋ - ⌊c ⟨-x⟩⌋`, where `⟨x⟩` is the
representative of `x` in `[0, 1)`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.OddPart.principalUnits B`: the units of `Ω` congruent to `1` modulo the maximal ideal of `B`,
  as an additive subgroup of `DiscreteUnits Ω`.
* `New.IsFrob B q σ`: `σ` stabilises `B`, and `σ x ≡ x ^ q` modulo the maximal ideal of `B` for
  every `x` in `B`; for `q = 1` this says that `σ` lies in the inertia group of `B`.
* `New.rootPowHom Ω m`: the map `ℤ/m → Ω^×`, `t ↦ ζᵗ`, for a fixed primitive `m`-th root of unity
  `ζ`; it is injective, and its image is the set of `m`-th roots of unity.
* `New.cyclotomicPowDirichlet l e ψ`: the character `cycᵉ ψ` of `Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)` with values in `Oˣ`,
  where `cyc` is the `l`-adic cyclotomic character.
modules.literature:
Known result: Kolyvagin's derivative classes of the Euler system of Gauss sums. Here the classes
carry a Tate twist and a Dirichlet character and are cocycles over the rationals that vanish at one
fixed element. Their ramification, the relation between Frobenius and inertia, and the link between
the bottom class and the Stickelberger element are also covered. Source: K. Rubin, Kolyvagin's
system of Gauss sums, Arithmetic Algebraic Geometry (Texel 1989), Progr. Math. 89, 1991, 309-324;
with a Tate twist: G. Banaszak, W. Gajda, Euler systems for higher K-theory of number fields, J.
Number Theory 58 (1996).

modules.title: Reciprocity laws and Stickelberger and Kolyvagin bounds for odd-part cocycles
modules.group: Kolyvagin cocycles, reciprocity laws and class bounds
modules.note:
The file studies cocycles on `Gal(Ω/ℚ)`, with `Ω` an algebraic closure of ℚ. Here
`New.cyclotomicPowDirichlet l e ψ` is `cyc^e ψ` with `cyc` the `l`-adic cyclotomic character. The
module `New.OddPart.component l e ψ ν` consists of the cocycles for `(cyc^e ψ)⁻¹` with values in
`O / l^ν`, where `O` (`PadicIntegerRing O l`) is the integer ring of a finite extension of ℚ_l, that
satisfy three conditions. They are unramified off `l` over ℚ(μ_N), split at `l` over ℚ(μ_{N l^∞})
and zero at `New.cmConj`, a complex conjugation. Reciprocity laws at primes `q ≡ 1` relate the value
of one cocycle at a Frobenius element to the ramification of another. Using these laws and
Chebotarev's theorem, the file bounds these components in two ways. One bound is an annihilation
result analogous to Stickelberger's theorem. The other uses Kolyvagin's descent with the Euler
system of Gauss sums.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.OddPart.artin_reciprocity_of_mem_component`: Artin reciprocity over ℚ(μ_{N m}), where the
  prime q ≡ 1 splits completely, pairs a cocycle `x` with a number `y`; only the places above q
  contribute.
* `New.OddPart.reciprocity_mod_ell`: the same law modulo `l` for a cocycle κ for cyc^(e+1) ψ; if
  `2 (a ^ e - 1) x φ ≠ 0`, then κ vanishes on the inertia group of `B`.
* `New.OddPart.nsmul_component_eq_zero`: if `X` has the Stickelberger property
  (`New.OddPart.IsStickelbergerBound N e X`), `cyc^e ψ` is odd and `e ≠ 0`, then `4 X²` kills
  `New.OddPart.component l e ψ ν` (an analogue of Stickelberger's theorem).
* `New.OddPart.exists_detecting_points_component`: for large `l`, a cocycle in
  `New.OddPart.component l e ψ ν` is determined by its values at `v_l(X) + 1` elements (Kolyvagin's
  descent with the Euler system of Gauss sums).

Notions from other files:
* `New.cyclotomicPowDirichlet l e ψ`: the character `cyc^e ψ` of `Gal(Ω/ℚ)` with values in `Oˣ`; the
  Dirichlet character `ψ` is read through the action on the `N`-th roots of unity.
* `New.OddPart.vanishingCocycles χ M s`: the `O`-module of locally constant maps `x : Gal(Ω/ℚ) → M`
  with `x (g h) = x g + χ(g) x h` (cocycles for `χ`) that vanish on `s`.
* `New.IsFrob A q σ`: `σ` stabilises the place `A` and `σ • x ≡ x ^ q` modulo its maximal ideal for
  all `x ∈ A`.
* `New.ordRat K A`: the order `Ωˣ → ℚ` at the place `A`, normalised to be `1` on uniformisers of
  `K`. `New.cyclotomicCharMod Ω n` gives the action on the `n`-th roots of unity, in `(ℤ/n)ˣ`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Stickelberger annihilation and the Kolyvagin–Rubin bound for odd twisted components.
Here the value is taken at a negative integer instead of at zero, and for an integer X whose
multiples (a^(e+1) − 1) X, for a ≡ 1 mod N, are congruent modulo each m prime to a to 2w times the
Stickelberger sum at level N m, and which for each prime ℓ is divisible by (a^e − 1)(a^(e+1) − 1)
for some such a prime to ℓ, 4X² kills the odd component at every prime. For large primes ℓ, at most
v_ℓ(X)+1 Galois elements detect its classes. Source: J. Coates, W. Sinnott, An analogue of
Stickelberger's theorem for the higher K-groups, Invent. Math. 24 (1974); K. Rubin, Euler Systems,
2000, III.4, Thm 4.6.
